newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chiwan expects boost from new berth, warehouse.
newsitem.headline: Chiwan expects boost from new berth, warehouse.

text.p: Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd expects its newly completed bulk cargo berth and grain warehouse to boost its profits in 1997, the company said in a news release on Friday.
The two projects, financed by proceeds from the company's offer of 40 million B shares at the end of 1995, were completed on Friday, it said.
The 85-million-yuan No.8 berth, with annual capacity of 1.20 million tonnes of bulk cargo, along with the 40,000-tonne grain warehouse, should buoy its profits in 1997, it said.
Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule next year and a recovery in the domestic economy should help toward Chiwan's profits next year, the company said but gave no earnings forecast.

In its interim report, the company said it posted audited net earnings of 56.06 million yuan in the first half of the year, compared with 62.31 million in the same 1995 period, under international accounting standards.

Chiwan blamed the earnings slide on increased competition in cargo handling in Shenzhen. Chiwan said it handled 2.68 million tonnes of bulk cargo in the first half of 1996, down 15.5 percent from 3.17 million tonnes in the same 1995 period.

The company said it expects earnings to pick up in the second half of this year, with Beijing expected to ease its tight control on credit, which should lead to an increase in bulk cargo shipped through Shenzhen.
